concepts.name: Disability types and web barriers
concepts.summary: Explain how visual, auditory, motor and cognitive disabilities, whether permanent, temporary or situational, lead to different barriers on web pages.

concepts.name: Assistive technology types
concepts.summary: Recall the main assistive technologies such as screen readers, magnifiers, switch devices and voice control, and what each does.

concepts.name: POUR principles
concepts.summary: Explain the four WCAG principles of Perceivable, Operable, Understandable and Robust with an example of each.

concepts.name: Text alternatives for images
concepts.summary: Understand why images need an alt attribute and what makes alt text useful versus redundant.

concepts.name: Headings and page structure
concepts.summary: Understand how heading levels give a page a navigable outline for screen reader users.

concepts.name: Keyboard-only operation
concepts.summary: Understand that all functionality must be usable with the keyboard alone, using Tab, Enter, Space and arrow keys.

concepts.name: Colour contrast basics
concepts.summary: Remember that text needs sufficient contrast with its background and that colour alone should not convey meaning.

misconceptions.text: Accessibility only matters for blind users.
Every image needs a long descriptive alt text.
Accessible pages must be plain, text-only versions of the site.

concepts.name: Semantic landmark elements
concepts.summary: Apply header, nav, main, aside and footer elements so assistive tech users can jump between page regions.

concepts.name: Decorative versus informative images
concepts.summary: Choose between descriptive alt text, empty alt and alternatives for functional images such as linked icons.

concepts.name: Accessible form labels
concepts.summary: Associate every form control with a visible label using label elements and group related controls with fieldset and legend.

concepts.name: Meaningful link text
concepts.summary: Write link text that makes sense out of context instead of phrases like click here.

concepts.name: Visible focus indication
concepts.summary: Keep or restyle the focus indicator so keyboard users can see where they are.

concepts.name: Native interactive elements
concepts.summary: Use button and a elements instead of clickable divs to get keyboard and role behaviour for free.

concepts.name: WCAG contrast ratios
concepts.summary: Check text and UI colours against WCAG ratio thresholds using a contrast tool.

concepts.name: Page language and title
concepts.summary: Understand why lang and a unique descriptive title help screen readers and navigation.

misconceptions.text: A placeholder can replace a visible label.
Removing the focus outline is fine because it looks cleaner.
A div with a click handler is as accessible as a button.

concepts.name: Accessible name computation
concepts.summary: Analyse how browsers derive an element's accessible name from content, labels and ARIA attributes.

concepts.name: ARIA roles and properties
concepts.summary: Apply ARIA roles, states and properties only where native HTML cannot express the semantics.

concepts.name: Focus order and management
concepts.summary: Keep DOM order logical, use tabindex 0 and -1 correctly and move focus programmatically for dialogs and route changes.

concepts.name: Accessible form errors
concepts.summary: Identify errors in text, link them to fields with aria-describedby and announce them to assistive tech.

concepts.name: Live regions for dynamic updates
concepts.summary: Use aria-live regions and status roles to announce content changes without moving focus.

concepts.name: Responsive and zoom support
concepts.summary: Analyse layouts for reflow at 400% zoom, text resizing and touch target size.

concepts.name: Motion and media alternatives
concepts.summary: Provide captions, transcripts and pause controls, and respect reduced-motion preferences.

concepts.name: WCAG conformance levels
concepts.summary: Distinguish levels A, AA and AAA and map success criteria to defects found on a page.

misconceptions.text: Positive tabindex values are a good way to set tab order.
Colour-only red borders are enough to signal form errors.

concepts.name: Custom widget keyboard patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse and implement expected keyboard interaction and ARIA states for tabs, menus, comboboxes and dialogs.

concepts.name: Manual screen reader testing
concepts.summary: Test flows with screen readers and keyboard, and interpret what announcements reveal about the accessibility tree.

concepts.name: Automated testing limits
concepts.summary: Evaluate what automated checkers can and cannot detect and combine them with manual review.

concepts.name: Accessibility tree inspection
concepts.summary: Use devtools to inspect roles, names and states and diagnose mismatches with the DOM.

concepts.name: Defect severity prioritisation
concepts.summary: Judge defects by user impact, affected journeys and WCAG level to prioritise remediation.

concepts.name: Accessible single-page apps
concepts.summary: Analyse how client-side routing and dynamic rendering break focus, titles and announcements, and fix them.

concepts.name: Cognitive accessibility patterns
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs for consistency, clear instructions, timeouts and error prevention that reduce cognitive load.

misconceptions.text: Passing an automated scan means a page is accessible.
If it works in one screen reader, it works in all of them.
Custom widgets are accessible once they have the right ARIA role.

concepts.name: Accessibility in design systems
concepts.summary: Design reusable components and tokens with built-in accessibility contracts, documentation and tests.

concepts.name: Accessibility process integration
concepts.summary: Build workflows that embed accessibility into requirements, design review, CI checks and release criteria.

concepts.name: Interpreting WCAG ambiguity
concepts.summary: Evaluate borderline cases against the intent of success criteria and justify conformance decisions.

concepts.name: Legal and conformance reporting
concepts.summary: Evaluate conformance evidence and produce accurate reports and statements referencing regulations such as the ADA, Section 508 and the EN 301 549 standard.

concepts.name: Usability testing with disabled users
concepts.summary: Plan and run research with disabled participants and turn findings into design change.

concepts.name: Assistive tech compatibility strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs and define a supported browser and assistive technology matrix, handling inconsistencies and workarounds.

concepts.name: Accessible complex data visualisation
concepts.summary: Create accessible alternatives for charts, maps and canvas content, such as data tables and descriptions.

misconceptions.text: Accessibility is a one-off audit done before launch.
A VPAT or conformance claim proves real-world usability.
A design system's accessible components guarantee accessible pages.
